units.text: The world is the closed rectangle `[0,length] × [0,width]`. Positions on its outer boundary are legal. Obstacle footprints include their boundaries and are forbidden to living agents. A path must remain entirely in traversable space; legal endpoints alone do not make a path legal. A dead agent's frozen historical position is not an occupancy constraint on a later gate operation; its remains are a separate spatial entity.

units.text: Agents are points in v0.1. They cannot pass through walls, but they do not physically collide with one another. Several agents can share a coordinate. This is a deliberate abstraction, so doorway crowding and body packing are not supported claims of this version. Shelters have no hard occupancy capacity. Body radii, congestion, and multi-floor space require a future ontology extension.

Repairing a breached gate yields an `OPEN` gate with positive integrity; closing is a separate action. A gate cannot close, or be repaired from breached, while a living agent occupies its footprint. Rebuilding a destroyed barricade requires a new build action and a new identity.

units.text: In v0.1 a barricade may fill a shelter's gate footprint only while that gate is `OPEN` or `BREACHED`. It becomes an independent barrier. The gate cannot close or be repaired from breached while an intact barricade overlaps its footprint. Barricade interiors cannot overlap other intact barrier interiors; sharing an edge is allowed. Their closed footprints cannot contain a nonempty stockpile or nonexhausted remains point. Existing living humans or zombies are never trapped inside newly created geometry.

units.text: Portable stocks use nonnegative integer quantities. Inventories have integer unit-mass capacity. A transfer is atomic: the same items leave one holder and enter another. Consumption and construction remove the specified quantity; no resource appears except in an initial condition, death-generated biomass, or a recorded intervention. There is no natural restocking, farming, resource decay, or stockpile movement in v0.1.

units.text: Signals propagate within their stated Euclidean radius through barriers. This is an explicit sound-like abstraction, not a sound physics model. A receiver must be alive and within radius at emission. The signal is delivered once; entering the radius later does not deliver it. units.text: Mitigated physical damage is `max(0, round_int(raw_damage × (1 - damage_resistance)))`. Actual damage is `min(current_life, mitigated_damage)`, and life after damage is `current_life - actual_damage`. Raw, mitigated, and actual damage are distinguishable in history. Healing uses `min(100, life + heal_amount)` and is only legal for a living eligible target. Starvation damage bypasses physical damage resistance.

units.text: Spitters start with 3 charges. Spending the first charge from a full reservoir schedules the next charge at resolution time + 30 s. At that deadline, a living Spitter gains one charge; if still below capacity, the next deadline is 30 s later, otherwise it is absent. Further expenditure does not postpone an already scheduled recharge. A missed spit spends a charge; a target-invalid attempt does not. Death or role removal terminates recharge.

units.text: Role attribute domains are explicit: ranges/radii are finite nonnegative reals in meters; durations, TTLs, and recharge intervals are finite positive reals in seconds; raw damage and repair/healing amounts are nonnegative integers; build integrity is a positive integer; item costs and maximum charges are positive integers; guard resistance is in [0,0.8]; prophylaxis resistance, spit potency, and rally hit bonus are in [0,1]; dash multiplier is a finite real >= 1. Common-property overrides retain their original domains. Spitter current charges range from 0 to its scenario's declared maximum; its next-charge time is present iff it is a living Spitter with an incomplete reservoir. All role properties are observed under the same rules as other current local game attributes. Only charge expenditure/recharge changes Spitter charge state during ordinary play.

An invalid target and a stochastic miss are different outcomes.

For this draft, “near-simultaneous” means **reciprocal direct attack occurrences whose active intervals overlap**: A attacks B while B is already attacking A, or vice versa. units.text: The first attack to reach a valid resolution wins the encounter; if both validly resolve at the same time, use the symmetric arbitration rule. Exactly one winning attempt may draw a hit and apply effects. The opposing overlapping attack is cancelled, even if the winning attempt misses or its damage is nonlethal. Its already spent stamina is not refunded. If a participant dies or converts, that lifecycle cancellation reason takes precedence over conflict cancellation.

With no eating, a human starting at hunger 20 reaches hunger 100 after 1,600 s, and first loses life to starvation at 1,610 s. units.text: **Case A — successful transmission without death.** A baseline zombie successfully bites an unprotected HEALTHY human at t=40. The human has life 80 and resistance to physical damage 0. Life becomes 74. Conditional infection probability is 0.36; suppose the recorded draw succeeds. The same human ID now has status INFECTED, onset 40, and deadline 340. Another bite at t=70 may damage the human but does not reset that deadline.

units.text: **Case B — cure and reinfection.** A Doctor starts treatment of that human at t=330 with one available medical supply. It completes at t=334, within range, while the human is alive and infected. The supply is consumed, the episode ends CURED, status becomes HEALTHY, and life remains 74 if no other event changed it. The former t=340 deadline has no effect. A new later successful exposure creates a different episode and deadline.

units.text: **Case C — treatment loses to the deadline.** Treatment instead starts at t=336 and would complete at t=340. Conversion at t=340 takes precedence. The human becomes a role-free Zombie with the same ID, current life/stamina, and position. Its inventory drops once. The Doctor's attempt fails on the now-ineligible target and releases its reserved medical item; its paid stamina is not refunded. The new zombie receives no cure from that attempt.

units.text: **Case E — reciprocal attacks cannot both kill.** An unarmored human with life 10 and a baseline zombie with life 10 begin opposing one-second melee/claw attacks at the same time. Arbitration chooses the human attempt. If it hits, 16 raw damage kills the zombie; the zombie's attack has no effects. If the human misses, the zombie's opposing attempt is still cancelled by the reciprocal-conflict rule, and neither loses life in this encounter. Subsequent fresh attacks are possible.

It was never part of that actor's inventory and is not dropped with its carried items.

V01: All other identity namespaces and cross-run links need broader coverage.
V02: Continuous trajectories and dynamic obstacles are not covered in full.
V03: Snapshot checks are covered; complete evolution is not.
V04: Only represented states/transitions are checked; omitted future behavior is not proved.
V05: Global episode overlap/history completeness remains partial.
V06: All host-death and duplicated lifecycle event cases are not exhaustively checked.
V07: Inventory drops, cancellations and model-memory resets are gaps.
V08: Assignments linked in snapshots are checked; full interval uniqueness is a gap.
V09: Complete contracts for all 29 actions are not enforced.
V10: General reservations and all interruption cases remain partial.
V11: Rate integration and timer recurrence are gaps.
V12: Global transfer/consumption conservation remains a gap outside selected treatment checks.
V13: Nonmedical reservation release and charge/biomass lifecycles remain partial.
V14: Endpoint checks cannot prove path legality or speed at every instant.
V15: Sensing/occlusion/memory privacy and feasibility information leakage are gaps.
V16: Actual random draws, sources, independence and their probability law are not validated.
V17: Physical damage and other healing arithmetic are not fully encoded.
V18: Lethal-hit ordering and reinfection transmission event laws remain a gap.
V19: Winner arbitration and target-invalid ordering still require behavioral verification.
V20: Occupancy/construction race effects are not checked in full.
V21: Exactly one remains per death and biomass creation/consumption histories are not fully checked.
V22: Continuous clocks, equal-time phase ordering and selection-frequency independence are not proved.
V23: baseline SHACL and independent RDF arithmetic/geometry checks
No complete initial agent placement or model execution is generated.
V24: Acyclicity is checked; completeness/replayability of the causal record is not proved.
V25: All derived speed/sensing/effect/armor calculations are not yet checked.
